A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GSASR and contain complete main papers and supplementary sections. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the methods, equations, tables, figures, and appendices.

before.justification: V3 reports original super-resolution experiments, image-quality metrics, runtime and memory measurements, qualitative comparisons, and ablations.

after.justification: V5 retains original empirical results and adds RGB-channel evaluations, rendering measurements, parameter ablations, and results for a larger GSASR variant.

M1.justification: The base GSASR pipeline is retained. Supplementary Section 7 adds an HAT-L variant using FlashAttention in the encoder and Gaussian decoder, with rotary positional embeddings replacing relative positional embeddings. These are limited architectural adaptations.

E1.justification: V5 adds SA-1B as a training corpus for the HAT-L variant, whereas v3 trains GSASR on DIV2K. The arbitrary-scale super-resolution task and eight evaluation datasets remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Matched benchmark and full-pipeline cost comparisons retain the same eight baselines. The new RGB and larger-model comparisons reuse LIIF, CiaoSR, and GaussianSR; the rendering-only comparison reuses GaussianSR. No comparator is added or removed within the retained comparisons.

E3.justification: V5 adds RGB-channel PSNR/SSIM evaluation and rendering-only cost measurement. Its HAT-L experiment uses 64×64 inputs, training scales sampled from [1,16], and mixed precision, versus the retained base setup's 48×48 inputs and [1,4] scales. Ablation settings also change: the Gaussian-count study replaces ×6 with ×8, rasterization tests replace r=0.05 with 0.01, and window-size tests omit k=10.

E4.justification: New supplementary Tables 16–17 test fixed versus learnable Gaussian positions and standard deviations. Existing Gaussian-count, rasterization, embedding-width, and window-size analyses are revised or expanded across scales and retained datasets. A rendering-only comparison additionally examines computational efficiency separately from the full pipeline.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Average runtime reporting over 100 image crops is retained without a new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: V5 adds RGB, rendering-only, parameter-ablation, and HAT-L results, and revises existing sensitivity results and timings. For example, CiaoSR's ×2 time in main Table 2 changes from 2,372 to 23,603 ms. Main Table 1 removes the EDSR DIV2K/LSDIR ×3, ×6, ×12, and ×18 result blocks without relocating those complete comparisons. HAT-L's Urban100 ×4 result of 28.44 dB uses changed training conditions and is not a same-setting improvement.

T1.justification: Supplementary Section 6.4 adds an O(d²N) complexity statement for the Gaussian interaction block's MLP layers to justify the embedding-width tradeoff. The Gaussian definitions, principal equations, rasterization algorithm, and existing complexity arguments remain mathematically equivalent; no new proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contributions: image-conditioned Gaussian prediction and efficient scale-aware CUDA rasterization for arbitrary-scale super-resolution. Rewritten advantages and additional experiments do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: V5 adds qualifications about excessive rasterization truncation and the computational cost of wider embeddings. It changes the window-size explanation from saturation beyond 12 to an accuracy–cost tradeoff, and discusses the larger variant's potential. The main limitations concerning Gaussian count, speed, and parameter burden remain.

D1.justification: Supplementary Section 7 documents the larger variant's precision, hardware, batch size, input size, optimizer, and learning-rate schedule, including 16 A100 GPUs and 500,000 iterations. Code/model access information is unchanged. A new r=1.0 statement in Section 6.3 conflicts with retained r=0.1 statements, making that setting less clear.

R1.justification: V5 adds citations for FlashAttention, rotary positional embeddings, Segment Anything, and two recent image-quality/super-resolution works. The GaussianSR discussion is rewritten around two explicit differences, but retains the earlier positioning concerning learnable Gaussian centers and efficient rasterization.

P1.justification: V5 makes localized grammar and terminology corrections, rewrites the advantages and GaussianSR comparison paragraphs, and clarifies window-size descriptions. Supplementary navigation expands from four sections to seven, while the main narrative and much of the existing explanatory text remain intact.

P2.justification: The supplementary tables expand from 12 to 18, with new RGB, rendering, parameter-ablation, and larger-model displays. Several existing ablation tables gain additional dataset and scale panels, and main Table 1 is condensed. Existing figures are retained but redistributed as the supplementary layout changes.

improvement.justification: The added RGB evaluations, rendering measurements, and direct parameter ablations strengthen empirical support for the existing method, while the larger variant has a documented training recipe. These gains are limited by new reporting inconsistencies: supplementary Section 6.3 contradicts the retained rasterization setting, and Table 17 duplicates the DIV2K ×4 values under LSDIR, conflicting with other LSDIR results. The useful additional evidence supports a modest overall improvement, with reduced confidence in those portions.
